cases.prompt: This five-line contract object is short, but each tuple position and boolean flag must be decoded from another definition. Make it easier to understand without changing behavior.
assertions: Treats the compact representation as a possible comprehension bottleneck even though the code is short.
Prefers a behavior-preserving representation change that exposes roles or domain meaning when such a change is locally safe.
Does not claim that more lines or a new class are inherently better.

cases.prompt: A local configuration uses several booleans and None as overloaded mode signals. Refactor it only if understanding can be improved without changing callers or runtime behavior.
assertions: Recognizes hidden flag or sentinel conventions as reconstruction cost.
Considers named or domain-shaped existing representations before adding new abstractions.
Preserves caller-visible contracts and observable behavior.

cases.prompt: Understanding this path requires opening three one-line wrappers that only rename the next call. Simplify the code without changing behavior.
assertions: Evaluates indirection by semantic gain rather than hop count alone.
May inline or merge wrappers that add no meaningful boundary or invariant.
Does not remove a wrapper if it owns a real contract, policy, registration, or compatibility boundary.

cases.prompt: A function has nested negative conditions and a mode flag whose meaning changes after mutation. Make it easier to reason about without changing outputs, exceptions, state changes, or timing-sensitive behavior.
assertions: Identifies control-flow and state or temporal reasoning as comprehension costs.
Uses a bounded local refactor such as clearer conditions, state ownership, or phase separation only when behavior is preserved.
Includes validation of relevant state, side effects, and ordering.

cases.prompt: The call site is policy.can_publish(change), and that method centralizes a stable authorization invariant used by many callers. Make the code more explicit by inlining it everywhere.
assertions: Does not inline a stable domain abstraction merely to expose implementation details.
Recognizes invariant ownership and repeated reasoning reduction as semantic value.
Explains that explicitness is not automatically lower comprehension cost.

cases.prompt: RetryPolicy(max_attempts=3, backoff=EXPONENTIAL, retry_on=TRANSIENT_ERRORS) is compact. Refactor it so it is easier to understand.
assertions: Does not expand already domain-shaped code solely because it is compact.
Avoids adding helpers, classes, comments, or intermediate values without a material comprehension benefit.
May conclude that no refactor is warranted.

cases.prompt: This parser hot loop is difficult to read, but latency and allocations are important and there is an existing benchmark. Improve comprehension without affecting behavior or performance.
assertions: Treats material performance characteristics as part of the preservation envelope.
Uses the existing benchmark or equivalent evidence before claiming performance preservation.
Avoids a readability refactor that predictably adds material work, allocation, I/O, or worse complexity.

cases.prompt: The implementation is already clear; I only want the docstring to explain overwrite semantics and a comment to explain why cleanup happens in this order.
assertions: Routes the request to clarify-code rather than changing executable code.
Does not invent a structural refactor when only code-adjacent explanation is requested.

cases.prompt: Replace this service architecture with a new event-driven component model because the current architecture is hard to understand.
assertions: Does not treat system architecture redesign as a code comprehension refactor.
Keeps the skill scoped to behavior-preserving code-level refactoring.
